title.zh: 卷二十四 志第四: 禮儀四
title.raw: 卷二十四 志第四: 禮儀四 Volume 24 Treatises 4: Rites 4

sentences.zh: 樂者，太古聖人治情之具也。

translations.literal: Music is the instrument whereby the utmost-ancient sages regulated emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Music was the tool the earliest sages used to govern the passions.

sentences.zh: 人有血氣生知之性，喜怒哀樂之情。

translations.literal: Humans have the nature of blood-and-breath and inborn knowing, and the sentiments of joy, anger, sorrow, and delight.
translations.idiomatic: People are born with blood and breath, with innate understanding—and with joy, anger, grief, and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 情感物而動於中，聲成文而應於外。

translations.literal: When emotion meets things it stirs within; when sound forms pattern it responds without.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling answers to the world inside; shaped sound answers outside.

sentences.zh: 聖王乃調之以律度，文之以歌頌，蕩之以鐘石，播之以弦管，然後可以滌精靈，可以祛怨思。

translations.literal: The sage-kings then tuned it with pitch standards, patterned it with songs and hymns, washed it with bells and stones, and spread it with strings and pipes—only then could the spirit be cleansed and resentful thoughts dispelled.
translations.idiomatic: The sage-kings set pitch to measure it, gave it words in praise, shook it through bronze and stone, breathed it through string and pipe—so the mind could be rinsed clean and brooding anger let go.

sentences.zh: 施之于邦國則朝廷序，施之於天下則神祇格，施之於賓宴則君臣和，施之于戰陣則士民勇。

translations.literal: Applied to the state, the court is ordered; applied to the realm, the spirits draw near; applied at guest banquets, lord and minister harmonize; applied on the battlefield, soldiers and people grow brave.
translations.idiomatic: Set it on a kingdom and the court falls into rank; set it on the world and gods and ghosts attend; set it at a feast and ruler and subject find accord; set it in the ranks and commoners and troops take heart.

sentences.zh: 三五之代，世有厥官，故虞廷振干羽之容，周人立弦誦之教。

translations.literal: In the eras of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors each generation had its officers; hence at Yu's court they raised the dance of shields and feathers, and among the Zhou they established the teaching of string and recitation.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors every age kept its music officers—so Shun's court revived the shield-and-feather dance, and the Zhou made plucked strings and choral learning a pillar of rule.

sentences.zh: 洎蒼精道喪，戰國塵飛，禮樂出於諸侯，《雅》、《頌》淪於衰俗。

translations.literal: When the azure essence's Way was lost and Warring States dust flew upward, ritual and music issued from feudal lords and the Odes and Hymns sank into a decadent age.
translations.idiomatic: Once the ancient order failed and the Warring States threw up their dust, rites and music belonged to whichever lord held power, and the Ya and Song odes were traded down into vulgar hands.

sentences.zh: 齊竽燕築，俱非皦繹之音；

translations.literal: The Qi zither and Yan zhu—neither was bright, pure sound;
translations.idiomatic: Qi's se and Yan's zhu—nothing left of clear, disciplined tone;

sentences.zh: 東缶西琴，各寫哇淫之狀。

translations.literal: east clay-vessel and west zither, each inscribed the look of wanton excess.
translations.idiomatic: eastern pot-drums and western lutes, each scoring out the shapes of lewd delight.

sentences.zh: 乃至播鞀入漢，師摯寢弦。

translations.literal: So far did it go that the bo drum entered Han and Master Zhi laid his strings to rest.
translations.idiomatic: It went so far that the war drum crossed into Han while Master Zhi let his strings fall silent.

sentences.zh: 延陵有自鄶之譏，孔子起聞《韶》之歎。

translations.literal: Yanling had the reproach of coming from Zheng; Confucius rose at hearing the Shao and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling Zi was mocked for music that smelled of Zheng; Confucius stood up when he heard the Shao and could only sigh.

sentences.zh: 及始皇一統，傲視百王。

translations.literal: When the First Emperor unified all, he looked down on the hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Shihuang welded the realm into one, he treated every earlier king as beneath notice.

sentences.zh: 鐘鼓滿于秦宮，無非鄭、衛；

translations.literal: Bells and drums filled the Qin palace—none but Zheng and Wei;
translations.idiomatic: The Qin palace rang wall to wall with bells and drums—and every piece was Zheng or Wei;

sentences.zh: 歌舞陳於漢廟，並匪《咸》、《韶》。

translations.literal: song and dance arrayed in the Han ancestral temple—none were Xian or Shao.
translations.idiomatic: song and dance lined the Han imperial temple—and none of it was the Xian or the Shao.

sentences.zh: 而九成、六變之容，八佾、四懸之制，但存其數，罕達其情。

translations.literal: Yet the forms of the Ninefold and the Six Changes, the institutions of eight rows and four suspended sets—only their numbers remained; rarely did their inner spirit reach through.
translations.idiomatic: The Ninefold rite and Six Changes survived as choreography; eight rows and four suspended choirs survived as numbers—but the feeling behind them scarcely arrived.

sentences.zh: 而制氏所傳，形容而已。

translations.literal: What the Music Office transmitted was mere outward description.
translations.idiomatic: All the Music Office handed on was outward shape.

sentences.zh: 武、宣之世，天子弘儒，采夜誦之詩，考從臣之賦，朝吟蘭殿，暮奏竹宮，乃命協律之官，始制禮神之曲。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Emperor Wu and Emperor Xuan the Son of Heaven enlarged Confucian learning, gathered poems recited at night, examined fu submitted by followers; morning chants in the Orchid Hall, evening performances at the Bamboo Palace—then he ordered the pitch-harmonizing officers and first fashioned hymns to honor the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han Wudi and Xuandi the throne championed the classics, collected night-recited verse and court poets' fu, sang mornings in the Orchid Hall and played evenings at the Bamboo Palace—then charged the pitch officers to compose the first sacral hymns.

sentences.zh: 屬河間好古，遺籍充庭，乃約《詩頌》而制樂章，體《周官》而為舞節。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Hejian loved antiquity and lost books filled his halls, he condensed the Poetry and Hymns to make musical chapters and took the Zhou Offices as model for dance sections.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Hejian hoarded old texts until his court overflowed with them; he trimmed the Odes and Hymns into scores and shaped dance sections after the Zhou Offices.

sentences.zh: 自茲相襲，代易其辭，雖流管磬之音，恐異《莖》、《英》之旨。

translations.literal: From then on the practice was handed down and each age changed the words; though pipe and chime tones flowed on, one feared they differed from the intent of Jing and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter each dynasty copied the form and swapped the words; pipes and stones still sounded, but the spirit of the Jing and Ying hymns was feared lost.

sentences.zh: 其後臥聽桑、濮，雜以《兜離》，孤竹、空桑，無復旋宮之義；

translations.literal: Later men listened reclining to Sang and Pu, mixed in with Doli; Guzhu and Kongsang—no more the principle of circulating the tonic;
translations.idiomatic: Later courts lolled to Sang of Pu and Doli mixed in; Guzhu and Kongsang pieces no longer obeyed circulating-tonic theory;

sentences.zh: 崇牙樹羽，惟陳備物之儀。

translations.literal: grand teeth and planted feathers—only the ritual of displaying equipage remained.
translations.idiomatic: tall tooth-boards and feather banners were all that was left—mere display of ritual gear.

sentences.zh: 煩手即多，知音蓋寡。

translations.literal: Many were the skilled hands; few were those who knew the tone.
translations.idiomatic: Players multiplied; true listeners grew scarce.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉之後，咸、洛為墟，禮壞樂崩，典章殆盡。

translations.literal: After the Yongjia era Xianyang and Luoyang became ruins; ritual collapsed and music shattered, and the canon was nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongjia the twin capitals turned to rubble; rites broke apart and music with them, and the written canon nearly vanished.

sentences.zh: 江左掇其遺散，尚有治世之音。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze they gathered the scattered remnants, and still had sounds of an ordered age.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangzuo states salvaged what scattered pieces they could and still kept something like music of a well-governed world.

sentences.zh: 而元魏、宇文，代雄朔漠，地不傳于清樂，人各習其舊風。

translations.literal: Yet Northern Wei and the house of Yuwen, dominating the northern deserts, did not transmit pure music in the land; each man practiced his old local style.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei and Yuwen's line ruled the northern steppe; clear court music did not take root there—every household kept its own frontier habit.

sentences.zh: 雖得兩京工胥，亦置四廂金奏。

translations.literal: Though they obtained craftsmen of the two capitals, they also set up the four-chamber metal performance.
translations.idiomatic: Even when they recruited artisans from Chang'an and Luoyang, they still staged the four-sided metal ensemble.

sentences.zh: 殊非入耳之玩，空有作樂之名。

translations.literal: Far from being pleasures for the ear, they had only the name of making music.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing in it pleased the ear; the title of court music was all that remained.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝家世士人，銳興禮樂，踐祚之始，詔太常卿牛弘、祭酒辛彥之增修雅樂。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui came from a scholar-official family and keenly revived ritual and music; at the start of his reign he decreed that Director of Court Music Niu Hong and Libationer Xin Yanzhi should augment and revise the elegant music.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Wendi rose from a literati house and threw himself into restoring rites and music; on taking the throne he ordered Court Music Director Niu Hong and Libationer Xin Yanzhi to rebuild the elegant repertoire.

sentences.zh: 弘集伶官，措思曆載無成，而郊廟侑神，黃鐘一調而已。

translations.literal: Hong assembled performing officers and labored at the problem for years without success; yet for suburban and temple offerings to the spirits, only the single Yellow Bell mode was used.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong gathered palace musicians and brooded over the task for years without finishing it; meanwhile suburban and temple rites made do with Yellow Bell alone.

sentences.zh: 平陳，始獲江左舊工及四懸樂器，帝令廷奏之，歎曰：「此華夏正聲也，非吾此舉，世何得聞。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified they first obtained the old craftsmen of the Jiangzuo and the four-suspended instruments; the Emperor ordered them performed at court and sighed, saying: "This is the correct sound of Huaxia; but for this act of mine, how would the world ever have heard it?
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell they finally gained Jiangzuo veterans and the four-suspended sets; Wendi had them played at court and exclaimed: "This is the true voice of the Central Lands—without my campaign, who alive would have heard it?

sentences.zh: 」乃調五音為五夏、二舞、登歌、房中等十四調，賓、祭用之。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Then he tuned the five notes into the five Summers, two dances, ascent hymn, inner-chamber suite, and the rest—fourteen suites in all—for guest rites and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The passage concluded." He then cast the five tones into fourteen court suites—the five Summers, two dances, ascent hymn, inner-chamber music, and the rest—for guest rites and sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 隋氏始有雅樂，因置清商署以掌之。

translations.literal: The Sui house first possessed elegant music and therefore established the Pure Shang Office to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the Sui possess a true elegant repertoire and found the Pure Shang Office to guard it.

sentences.zh: 既而協律郎祖孝孫依京房舊法，推五音十二律為六十音，又六之，有三百六十音，旋相為宮，因定廟樂。

translations.literal: Thereafter Pitch-Harmonizing Gentleman Zu Xiaosun, following Jing Fang's old method, derived five notes and twelve pitches into sixty tones, then multiplied by six to make three hundred sixty tones, circulating the tonic in turn, and thereby fixed the temple music.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Pitch Officer Zu Xiaosun, using Jing Fang's old arithmetic, stretched five tones and twelve pitches into sixty notes, then sixfold into three hundred sixty, cycling the tonic through the year—and so drafted temple music on paper.

sentences.zh: 諸儒論難，竟不施用。

translations.literal: The Confucian scholars debated and objected; in the end it was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Ru scholars quarreled over it until the scheme was shelved.

sentences.zh: 隋世雅音，惟清樂十四調而已。

translations.literal: Elegant sound in the Sui age was only the fourteen suites of pure music.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, court elegance meant those fourteen pure-music suites—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 隋末大亂，其樂猶全。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui great disorder came, yet the music remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Sui collapsed in chaos, but the scores and instruments survived.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，擢祖孝孫為吏部郎中，轉太常少卿，漸見親委。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the Mandate he promoted Zu Xiaosun to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then transferred him to Vice Director of Court Music, and gradually drew him into close trust.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Gaozu took the throne he raised Zu Xiaosun to a post in the Ministry of Personnel, then made him Vice Director of Court Music and steadily leaned on him.

sentences.zh: 孝孫由是奏請作樂。

translations.literal: Xiaosun thereby memorialized requesting the making of music.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Xiaosun seized the moment and asked leave to compose new state music.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多務，未遑改創，樂府尚用隋氏舊文。

translations.literal: At the time military and state affairs were many; there was no leisure to reform and create anew, and the Music Office still used the Sui house's old scores.
translations.idiomatic: Armies and administration consumed the court; reform waited, and the Music Office still performed from Sui books.

sentences.zh: ，始命孝孫修定雅樂，至六月奏之。

translations.literal: , then first ordered Xiaosun to revise and fix the elegant music; by the sixth month it was presented.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 9 he finally charged Zu Xiaosun to overhaul the elegant repertoire; by the sixth month of Zhenguan 2 it was ready for the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「禮樂之作，蓋聖人緣物設教，以為撙節，治之隆替，豈此之由？

translations.literal: Taizong said: "The making of ritual and music—surely the sages, encountering things, set up teaching and used it as restraint; whether rule rises or falls, can it really depend on this?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "Rites and music exist because sages read the world and taught through it—to brace conduct. Whether a reign flourishes or fails, can bells and hymns really be the cause?

sentences.zh: 」御史大夫杜淹對曰：「前代興亡，實由於樂。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Censor-in-Chief Du Yan replied: "The rise and fall of former ages truly lay in music.
translations.idiomatic: The passage concluded." Censor-in-Chief Du Yan answered: "Former dynasties rose and fell through music—that much is plain.

sentences.zh: 陳將亡也，為《玉樹後庭花》；

translations.literal: When Chen was about to perish they made Jade Tree in the Rear Court;
translations.idiomatic: Chen on the brink composed Jade Tree in the Rear Court;

sentences.zh: 齊將亡也，而為《伴侶曲》。

translations.literal: when Qi was about to perish they made the Companion Song.
translations.idiomatic: Qi on the brink composed the Companion Song.

sentences.zh: 行路聞之，莫不悲泣，所謂亡國之音也。

translations.literal: Travelers on the road who heard them all wept—what were called the tunes of a perishing state.
translations.idiomatic: Wayfarers who heard them wept in the street—the so-called music of a dying kingdom.

sentences.zh: 以是觀之，蓋樂之由也。

translations.literal: Viewed in this light, surely music is the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Seen that way, music is the lever of fate.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「不然，夫音聲能感人，自然之道也。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "It is not so: sound can move people—that is nature's way.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "No. Sound moves the heart—that is nature.

sentences.zh: 故歡者聞之則悅，憂者聽之則悲，悲歡之情，在於人心，非由樂也。

translations.literal: Hence the joyful hear it and are pleased; the sorrowful hear it and are grieved; the sentiments of grief and joy lie in the human heart, not in the music.
translations.idiomatic: The glad listener brightens; the grieving listener breaks—the feeling lives in the listener, not in the tune.

sentences.zh: 將亡之政，其民必苦，然苦心所感，故聞之則悲耳，何有樂聲哀怨，能使悅者悲乎？

translations.literal: A government about to perish—its people must be bitter; it is the bitter heart that responds, so on hearing they grieve. How could a plaintive tone in the music make the pleased become grieved?
translations.idiomatic: A state about to fall breeds a bitter people; bitterness answers to the ear, and the tune sounds sad. What plaint in the score could force a happy man to weep?

sentences.zh: 今《玉樹》、《伴侶》之曲，其聲具存，朕當為公奏之，知公必不悲矣。

translations.literal: Now the tunes Jade Tree and Companion still survive in full; I shall play them for you, and I know you will not grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Jade Tree and Companion still survive intact. I will play them for you—and you will not weep.

sentences.zh: 」尚書右丞魏徵進曰：「古人稱：『禮云禮云，玉帛云乎哉！

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Wei Zheng advanced, saying: "The ancients said: 'Rites, rites—is it jade and silk they mean!
translations.idiomatic: The passage concluded." Secretariat Vice Director Wei Zheng stepped forward: "The ancients said, 'Rites, rites—are we talking about jade and silk?

sentences.zh: 樂云樂云，鐘鼓云乎哉！

translations.literal: Music, music—is it bells and drums they mean!
translations.idiomatic: Music, music—are we talking about bells and drums?

sentences.zh: 』樂在人和，不由音調。

translations.literal: ' Music lies in the harmony of people, not in pitch. The passage concluded." The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: ' Music is the harmony among people, not the scale. The passage concluded." Taizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 」太宗然之。

translations.literal: Taizong assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his point.

sentences.zh: 孝孫又奏：「陳、梁舊樂，雜用吳、楚之音；

translations.literal: Xiaosun again memorialized: "The old music of Chen and Liang mixed Wu and Chu tones;
translations.idiomatic: Zu Xiaosun memorialized again: "Chen and Liang scores still carry Wu and Chu color;

sentences.zh: 周、齊舊樂，多涉胡戎之伎。

translations.literal: the old music of Zhou and Qi largely involved barbarian frontier pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Qi scores lean on northern and frontier pieces.

sentences.zh: 於是斟酌南北，考以古音，作為大唐雅樂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he weighed north and south, examined against ancient sound, and made the Great Tang elegant music.
translations.idiomatic: He weighed north against south, tested both against ancient pitch, and forged the Great Tang elegant repertoire.

sentences.zh: 以十二律各順其月，旋相為宮。

translations.literal: With the twelve pitches each following its month, he circulated the tonic in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pitches aligned to the months; the tonic cycled through the year.

sentences.zh: 按《禮記》云『大樂與天地同和』，故制十二和之樂，合三十一曲，八十四調。

translations.literal: According to the Record of Rites, 'Great music is of one harmony with Heaven and Earth'; therefore he fashioned music of twelve harmonies, altogether thirty-one pieces and eighty-four modes.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says great music shares heaven and earth's harmony—so he built twelve harmonic suites: thirty-one pieces, eighty-four modes.

sentences.zh: 祭圓丘以黃鐘為宮，方澤以林鐘為宮，宗廟乙太簇為宮。

translations.literal: For the round-altar sacrifice to Heaven, Yellow Bell served as tonic; for the square-mound sacrifice to Earth, Forest Bell; for the ancestral temple, Great Cluster.
translations.idiomatic: Round Mound rites took Yellow Bell as tonic; Square Mound rites Forest Bell; ancestral temples Great Cluster.

sentences.zh: 五郊、朝賀、饗宴，則隨月用律為宮。

translations.literal: For the five suburban altars, court congratulations, and feasts, then according to the month the appropriate pitch served as tonic.
translations.idiomatic: For the five suburban altars, court audiences, and banquets, the month's pitch ruled the tonic.

sentences.zh: 」初，隋但用黃鐘一宮，惟扣七鐘，餘五鐘虛懸而不扣。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." At first Sui used only the single Yellow Bell tonic, striking only seven bells while the other five bells hung empty and were not struck.
translations.idiomatic: The passage concluded." Earlier Sui had used Yellow Bell alone, striking seven bells while five hung mute on the rack.

sentences.zh: 及孝孫建旋宮之法，皆遍扣鐘，無復虛懸者矣。

translations.literal: When Xiaosun established the method of circulating the tonic, all bells were struck in turn; none hung empty any longer.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zu Xiaosun restored circulating-tonic practice, every bell on the rack sounded; none was left idle.

sentences.zh: 祭天神奏《豫和》之樂，地祇奏《順和》，宗廟奏《永和》。

translations.literal: For sacrifices to the celestial spirit they played the Yuhe suite; for earth spirits the Shunhe; for the ancestral temple the Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven rites used Yuhe; earth rites Shunhe; ancestral temples Yonghe.

sentences.zh: 天地、宗廟登歌，俱奏《肅和》。

translations.literal: For heaven, earth, and ancestral temple ascent hymns, all played Suhe.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent hymns at heaven, earth, and temple alike used Suhe.

sentences.zh: 皇帝臨軒，奏《太和》。

translations.literal: When the Emperor faced the hall they played Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne hall, Taihe sounded.

sentences.zh: 王公出入，奏《舒和》。

translations.literal: When princes and dukes entered or left, Shuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and dukes entering or leaving heard Shuhe.

sentences.zh: 皇帝食舉及飲酒，奏《休和》。

translations.literal: When the Emperor raised food or drank wine, Xiuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial meals and toasts used Xiuhe.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受朝，奏《政和》。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received court, Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial audiences used Zhenghe.

sentences.zh: 皇太子軒懸出入，奏《承和》。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince with full suspended bells entered or left, Chenghe.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's full bell-set processions used Chenghe.

sentences.zh: 元日，冬至皇帝禮會登歌，奏《昭和》。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day and the winter solstice, when the Emperor's ritual assembly ascent hymn was performed, Zhaohe.
translations.idiomatic: New Year and winter-solstice state rites sang Zhaohe at the ascent hymn.

sentences.zh: 郊廟俎入，奏《雍和》。

translations.literal: When suburban and temple offering-trays entered, Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: When offering trays entered at suburban or temple rites, Yonghe.

sentences.zh: 皇帝祭享酌酒、讀祝文及飲福、受胙，奏《壽和》。

translations.literal: When the Emperor at sacrificial offerings poured wine, read the prayer text, drank the blessing cup, and received the sacrificial flesh, Shouhe.
translations.idiomatic: Pouring the libation, reading the prayer, drinking the blessing cup, receiving the sacrificial meat—Shouhe accompanied each.

sentences.zh: 五郊迎氣，各以月律而奏其音。

translations.literal: For welcoming the qi at the five suburban altars, each played its sound according to the monthly pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The five suburban qi-welcoming rites each took the month's pitch for its tone.

sentences.zh: 又郊廟祭享，奏《化康》、《凱安》之舞。

translations.literal: Again for suburban and temple sacrifices they danced the Huakang and Kaian suites.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban and temple sacrifices also danced Huakang and Kaian.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》旋宮之義，亡絕已久，時莫能知，一朝復古，自此始也。

translations.literal: The meaning of circulating the tonic in the Rites of Zhou had long been extinct; none of the age could know it—restoring antiquity in a single morning began here.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou ritual's circulating tonic had been dead for ages; no one alive understood it until one morning brought it back—here was the start.

sentences.zh: 及孝孫卒後，協律郎張文收復采《三禮》，言孝孫雖創其端，至於郊禋用樂，事未周備。

translations.literal: After Xiaosun died, Pitch-Harmonizing Gentleman Zhang Wenshou again gathered the Three Rites and said that though Xiaosun had opened the path, as to music used at suburban and border sacrifices the matter was not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: After Zu Xiaosun's death, Pitch Officer Zhang Wenshou mined the Three Rites and argued that Xiaosun had only opened the work—suburban and border-sacrifice music still needed finishing.

sentences.zh: 詔文收與太常掌禮樂官等更加厘改。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wenshou and the Court Music officers in charge of ritual music jointly to revise further.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Zhang Wenshou and the Court Music ritual officers to revise the system together.

sentences.zh: 於是依《周禮》，祭昊天上帝以圓鐘為宮，黃鐘為角，太簇為徵，姑洗為羽，奏《豫和》之舞。

translations.literal: Thereupon according to the Rites of Zhou, for sacrifice to August Heaven and God the round bell served as tonic, Yellow Bell as angle, Great Cluster as mode, Guxian as feather, and they danced the Yuhe suite.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Zhou Offices: August Heaven took round bell as tonic, Yellow Bell as second, Great Cluster as third, Guxian as fifth, with the Yuhe dance.

sentences.zh: 若封太山，同用此樂。

translations.literal: If enfeoffing Mount Tai, the same music was used.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Tai enfeoffment used the same score.

sentences.zh: 若地祇方丘，以函鐘為宮，太簇為角，姑洗為徵，南呂為羽，奏《順和》之舞。

translations.literal: If earth spirits at the square mound, the sealed bell as tonic, Great Cluster as angle, Guxian as mode, Southern Lu as feather, dancing the Shunhe suite.
translations.idiomatic: Earth at the Square Mound: sealed bell tonic, Great Cluster second, Guxian third, Southern Lu fifth, Shunhe dance.

sentences.zh: 禪梁甫，同用此樂。

translations.literal: The Liangfu shan solemn rite employed this music as well.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn rites at Liangfu shared the same score.

sentences.zh: 祫禘宗廟，以黃鐘為宮，大呂為角，太簇為徵，應鐘為羽，奏《永和》之舞。

translations.literal: For the collective ancestral temple rite, Yellow Bell as tonic, Great Lu as angle, Great Cluster as mode, Ying Bell as feather, dancing the Yonghe suite.
translations.idiomatic: Collective ancestral rites: Yellow Bell tonic, Great Lu second, Great Cluster third, Ying Bell fifth, Yonghe dance.

sentences.zh: 五郊、日月星辰及類于上帝，黃鐘為宮，奏《豫和》之曲。

translations.literal: For the five suburban altars, sun, moon, stars, and the rite categorizing spirits with God, Yellow Bell as tonic, playing the Yuhe suite.
translations.idiomatic: Five suburban altars, sun, moon, stars, and spirits classed with Heaven: Yellow Bell tonic, Yuhe suite.

sentences.zh: 大蠟、大報，以黃鐘、太簇、姑洗、蕤賓、夷則、無射等調奏《豫和》、《順和》、《永和》之曲。

translations.literal: For the great La and great Report rites, the modes Yellow Bell, Great Cluster, Guxian, Flabby Guest, Yi Ze, and Wushe played the Yuhe, Shunhe, and Yonghe suites.
translations.idiomatic: Great La and Great Report rites cycled Yellow Bell, Great Cluster, Guxian, Flabby Guest, Yi Ze, and Wushe through Yuhe, Shunhe, and Yonghe.

sentences.zh: 明堂、雩，以黃鐘為宮，奏《豫和》之曲。

translations.literal: For the Bright Hall and rain-prayer rites, Yellow Bell as tonic, playing the Yuhe suite.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall and rain-prayer rites: Yellow Bell tonic, Yuhe suite.

sentences.zh: 神州、社稷、藉田，宜乙太簇為宮，雨師以姑洗為宮，山川以蕤賓為宮，並奏《順和》之曲。

translations.literal: For the Central Land, altars of soil and grain, and plowing rites, Great Cluster should serve as tonic; for the Rain Master Guxian; for mountains and rivers Flabby Guest—and all played the Shunhe suite.
translations.idiomatic: Central Land, soil-and-grain altars, and plowing rites took Great Cluster; Rain Master Guxian; mountains and rivers Flabby Guest—all with Shunhe.

sentences.zh: 饗先妣，以夷則為宮，奏《永和》之舞。

translations.literal: For feasting the late queen-mother, Yi Ze as tonic, dancing the Yonghe suite.
translations.idiomatic: Feasts for the deceased empress dowager: Yi Ze tonic, Yonghe dance.

sentences.zh: 大饗宴，奏姑洗、蕤賓二調。

translations.literal: At the great feast, the Guxian and Flabby Guest modes.
translations.idiomatic: Grand banquets used Guxian and Flabby Guest modes.

sentences.zh: 皇帝郊廟、食舉，以月律為宮，並奏《休和》之曲。

translations.literal: When the Emperor at suburban and temple rites raised food, the monthly pitch as tonic, all playing the Xiuhe suite.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial ritual meals at suburban or temple rites took the month's pitch and played Xiuhe.

sentences.zh: 皇帝郊廟出入，奏《太和》之樂，臨軒出入，奏《舒和》之樂，並以姑洗為宮。

translations.literal: When the Emperor entered or left at suburban and temple rites, the Taihe suite; when entering or leaving the throne hall, the Shuhe suite—all with Guxian as tonic.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial processions at suburban temples used Taihe; throne-hall processions Shuhe—both with Guxian as tonic.

sentences.zh: 皇帝大射，姑洗為宮，奏《騶虞》之曲。

translations.literal: When the Emperor performed the great archery rite, Guxian as tonic, playing the Zouyu suite.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial great archery: Guxian tonic, Zouyu suite.

sentences.zh: 皇太子奏《狸首》之曲。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince played the Lishou suite.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's archery used Lishou.

sentences.zh: 皇太子軒懸，姑洗為宮，奏《永和》之曲。

translations.literal: For the Crown Prince's full suspended set, Guxian as tonic, playing the Yonghe suite.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's full bell procession: Guxian tonic, Yonghe suite.

sentences.zh: 凡奏黃鐘，歌大呂；

translations.literal: When Yellow Bell was played, Great Lu was sung;
translations.idiomatic: Strike Yellow Bell, sing Great Lu;

sentences.zh: 奏太簇，歌應鐘；

translations.literal: when Great Cluster was played, Ying Bell was sung;
translations.idiomatic: strike Great Cluster, sing Ying Bell;

sentences.zh: 奏姑洗，歌南呂；

translations.literal: when Guxian was played, Southern Lu was sung;
translations.idiomatic: strike Guxian, sing Southern Lu;

sentences.zh: 奏蕤賓，歌林鐘；

translations.literal: when Flabby Guest was played, Forest Bell was sung;
translations.idiomatic: strike Flabby Guest, sing Forest Bell;

sentences.zh: 奏夷則，歌中呂；

translations.literal: when Yi Ze was played, Middle Lu was sung;
translations.idiomatic: strike Yi Ze, sing Middle Lu;

sentences.zh: 奏無射，歌夾鐘。

translations.literal: when Wushe was played, Pinched Bell was sung.
translations.idiomatic: strike Wushe, sing Pinched Bell.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘蕤賓為宮，其樂九變；

translations.literal: With Huangzhong and Ruibin as palace-tonic, its music has nine changes;
translations.idiomatic: With Huangzhong and Ruibin as the palace-tonic, the music has nine variations;

sentences.zh: 大呂、林鐘為宮，其樂八變。

translations.literal: With Dalü and Linzhong as palace-tonic, its music has eight changes.
translations.idiomatic: With Dalü and Linzhong as the palace-tonic, the music has eight variations.

sentences.zh: 太簇、夷則為宮，其樂七變。

translations.literal: With Taizu and Yize as palace-tonic, its music has seven changes.
translations.idiomatic: With Taizu and Yize as the palace-tonic, the music has seven variations.

sentences.zh: 夾鐘、南呂為宮，其樂六變。

translations.literal: With Jiazhong and Nanlü as palace-tonic, its music has six changes.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiazhong and Nanlü as the palace-tonic, the music has six variations.

sentences.zh: 姑洗、無射為宮，其樂五變。

translations.literal: With Guqian and Wushe as palace-tonic, its music has five changes.
translations.idiomatic: With Guqian and Wushe as the palace-tonic, the music has five variations.

sentences.zh: 中呂、應鐘為宮，其樂四變。

translations.literal: With Zhonglü and Yingzhong as palace-tonic, its music has four changes.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhonglü and Yingzhong as the palace-tonic, the music has four variations.

sentences.zh: 天子十二鐘，上公九，侯伯七，子男五，卿六，大夫四，士三。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had twelve bells; upper dukes nine, marquises and earls seven, viscounts and barons five, ministers six, grand masters four, knights three.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven had twelve bells; upper dukes nine, marquises and earls seven, viscounts and barons five, ministers six, grand masters four, and knights three.

sentences.zh: 及成，奏之。

translations.literal: When it was completed, it was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, it was performed.

sentences.zh: 太宗稱善，於是加級頒賜各有差。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor praised it; thereupon ranks were raised and gifts distributed, each according to difference.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor praised it; ranks were then raised and gifts distributed according to merit.

sentences.zh: 十四年，敕曰：「殷薦祖考，以崇功德，比雖加以誠潔，而廟樂未稱。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, an edict said: "Yin offered to ancestors and fathers to exalt merit and virtue; though we have lately added sincerity and purity, the temple music is still unfitting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year an edict said: "Yin offered to ancestors and fathers to exalt merit and virtue; though we have lately added sincerity and purity, the temple music is still unfitting.

sentences.zh: 宜令所司詳諸故實，制定奏聞。

translations.literal: Let the responsible offices examine the former precedents in detail, fix regulations, and memorialize for approval."
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible offices examine former precedents in detail, fix regulations, and submit a memorial for approval."

sentences.zh: 」八座議曰：「七廟觀德，義冠于宗祀；

translations.literal: The Eight Seats deliberated, saying: "The seven temples display virtue; their meaning crowns ancestral sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Seats deliberated: "The seven temples display virtue; their meaning crowns ancestral sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 三祖在天，式章于嚴配。

translations.literal: the three ancestors in Heaven manifest it in solemn pairing.
translations.idiomatic: the three ancestors in Heaven display it in solemn pairing.

sentences.zh: 致敬之情允洽，大孝之道宜宣。

translations.literal: The sentiment of reverence is fully harmonized; the way of great filial piety should be proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Reverence is fully harmonized; the way of great filial piety should be proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 是以八佾具陳，肅儀形於綴兆；

translations.literal: Therefore the eight rows are fully arrayed, and the solemn rites take form in the dance positions;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the eight rows are fully arrayed, and solemn rites take form in the dance positions;

sentences.zh: 四懸備展，被鴻徽於雅音。

translations.literal: the four suspensions are fully deployed, spreading the great emblem in elegant tones.
translations.idiomatic: the four suspensions are fully deployed, spreading the great emblem through elegant tones.

sentences.zh: 考作樂之明義，擇皇王之令典，前聖所履，莫大於茲。

translations.literal: Examining the bright meaning of making music and selecting the august kings' proper canons—what former sages practiced, nothing is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: To examine the bright meaning of making music and select the august kings' proper canons—among what former sages practiced, nothing is greater.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下，天縱感通，率由冥極。

translations.literal: We bow before Your Majesty the Emperor, Heaven-endowed with sympathetic penetration, following the dark ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: We bow before Your Majesty, Heaven-endowed with sympathetic penetration, following the dark ultimate.

sentences.zh: 孝理昭懿，光被於八埏；

translations.literal: Filial governance is manifest and brilliant, shining over the eight directions;
translations.idiomatic: Filial governance is manifest and brilliant, shining across the realm;

sentences.zh: 愛敬純深，追崇于百葉。

translations.literal: love and reverence pure and deep, pursuing honor through a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: love and reverence pure and deep, pursuing honor for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 永言錫祚，斯弘頌聲。

translations.literal: Everlasting words bestow blessing; thereby the eulogistic voice is magnified.
translations.idiomatic: Everlasting words bestow blessing; thereby praise is magnified.

sentences.zh: 鐘律革音，播鏗鏘於饗薦；

translations.literal: Bell-tones change their notes, spreading clangor in offerings;
translations.idiomatic: Bell-tones change their notes, spreading clangor at offerings;

sentences.zh: 羽籥成列，申蹈厲於烝嘗。

translations.literal: feather-flutes form their ranks, displaying vigorous tread in seasonal and ancestral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: feather-flutes form their ranks, displaying vigorous tread at seasonal and ancestral sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 爰詔典司，乃加隆稱，循聲核實，敬闡尊名。

translations.literal: Thereupon edicts went to the canonical offices, and elevated titles were added; following the sound and verifying the substance, we respectfully clarify honored names.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts then went to the canonical offices and elevated titles were added; following the sound and verifying the substance, we respectfully clarify honored names.

sentences.zh: 竊以皇靈滋慶，浚源長委，邁吞燕之生商，軼擾龍之肇漢，盛韜光於九二，漸發跡於三分。

translations.literal: We venture that the imperial numen increases blessing; the deep source long pours forth, surpassing Yan's swallowing of Shang and exceeding the dragon-disturbing founding of Han, storing brilliance in the nine-twos and gradually issuing forth at the three divisions.
translations.idiomatic: We venture that the imperial numen increases blessing; the deep source long pours forth, surpassing Yan's swallowing of Shang and exceeding the dragon-disturbing founding of Han, storing brilliance in concealment and gradually issuing forth at the three divisions.

sentences.zh: 高祖縮地補天，重張區宇，反魂肉骨，再造生靈。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor drew in earth and patched heaven, again spreading the realm's bounds, returning souls to flesh and bones, again creating living beings.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor drew in earth and patched heaven, again spreading the realm's bounds, returning souls to flesh and bone, again creating the living.

sentences.zh: 恢恢帝圖，與二儀而合大；

translations.literal: Vast is the imperial design, joining with the two regulators in greatness;
translations.idiomatic: Vast is the imperial design, joining heaven and earth in greatness;

sentences.zh: 赫赫皇道，共七曜以齊明。

translations.literal: splendid is the imperial way, together with the seven luminaries in brightness.
translations.idiomatic: splendid is the imperial way, matching the seven luminaries in brightness.

sentences.zh: 雖復聖跡神功，不可得而窺測；

translations.literal: Though sage traces and divine achievements cannot be fathomed by scrutiny;
translations.idiomatic: Though sage traces and divine achievements cannot be fathomed;

sentences.zh: 經文緯武，敢有寄于名言。

translations.literal: the warp of culture and woof of arms—we dare lodge them in famous words.
translations.idiomatic: the warp of culture and woof of arms—we dare set them down in famous words.

sentences.zh: 敬備樂章，式昭彝範。

translations.literal: Respectfully preparing music sections to display the constant pattern.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully prepare music sections to display the constant pattern.

sentences.zh: 皇祖弘農府君、宣簡公、懿王三廟樂，請同奏《長發》之舞。

translations.literal: For the temples of Imperial Grandfather Hongnong, Xuanjian Duke, and Illustrious King, the music should jointly perform the dance "Changfa."
translations.idiomatic: For the temples of Imperial Grandfather Hongnong, Duke Xuanjian, and Illustrious King, the music should jointly perform the dance Changfa.

sentences.zh: 太祖景皇帝廟樂，請奏《大基》之舞。

translations.literal: For the Founding Ancestor Emperor Jing's temple music, please perform the dance "Daji."
translations.idiomatic: For the Founding Ancestor Emperor Jing's temple music, please perform the dance Daji.

sentences.zh: 世祖元皇帝廟樂，請奏《大成》之舞。

translations.literal: For the World Ancestor Emperor Yuan's temple music, please perform the dance "Dacheng."
translations.idiomatic: For the World Ancestor Emperor Yuan's temple music, please perform the dance Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖大武皇帝廟樂，請奏《大明》之舞。

translations.literal: For the High Ancestor Great Martial Emperor's temple music, please perform the dance "Daming."
translations.idiomatic: For the High Ancestor Great Martial Emperor's temple music, please perform the dance Daming.

sentences.zh: 文德皇后廟樂，請奏《光大》之舞。

translations.literal: For the Cultured Virtue Empress's temple music, please perform the dance "Guangda."
translations.idiomatic: For the Cultured Virtue Empress's temple music, please perform the dance Guangda.

sentences.zh: 七廟登歌，請每室別奏。

translations.literal: For the seven temples' ascent hymns, please perform separately in each chamber."
translations.idiomatic: For the seven temples' ascent hymns, please perform a separate piece in each chamber."

sentences.zh: 」制可之。

translations.literal: The ordinance approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，太尉長孫無忌、侍中于志寧議太宗廟樂曰：「《易》曰：『先王作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Grand Mentor Zhangsun Wuji and Palace Attendant Yu Zhining deliberated on the Founding Ancestor's temple music, saying: "The Changes says: 'Former kings made music to exalt virtue, Yin offered to the Supreme Lord, to pair with ancestors and fathers.'
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Grand Mentor Zhangsun Wuji and Palace Attendant Yu Zhining deliberated on the Founding Ancestor's temple music: "The Changes says, 'Former kings made music to exalt virtue; Yin offered to the Supreme Lord to pair with ancestors and fathers.'

sentences.zh: 』請樂名《崇德》之舞。

translations.literal: We request the music be named the dance "Chongde."
translations.idiomatic: We request the music be named the dance Chongde.

sentences.zh: 」制可之。

translations.literal: The ordinance approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 後文德皇后廟，有司據禮停《光大》之舞，惟進《崇德》之舞。

translations.literal: Later, at the Cultured Virtue Empress's temple, the offices according to ritual stopped the dance "Guangda" and advanced only the dance "Chongde."
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the Cultured Virtue Empress's temple, the offices by ritual stopped the dance Guangda and advanced only the dance Chongde.

sentences.zh: 九月，高宗廟樂，以《鈞天》為名。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the High Ancestor's temple music took "Juntian" as its name.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the High Ancestor's temple music took Juntian as its name.

sentences.zh: 中宗廟樂，奏《太和》之舞。

translations.literal: The Middle Ancestor's temple music performed the dance "Taihe."
translations.idiomatic: The Middle Ancestor's temple music performed the dance Taihe.

sentences.zh: 十月敕，睿宗廟奏《景雲》之舞。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict: at the Sagacious Ancestor's temple perform the dance "Jingyun."
translations.idiomatic: A tenth-month edict ordered the Sagacious Ancestor's temple to perform the dance Jingyun.

sentences.zh: 二十九年六月，太常奏：「准十二年東封太山日所定雅樂，其樂曰《元和》六變，以降天神。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-ninth year, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized: "According to the elegant music fixed on the day of the eastern feng at Mount Tai in the twelfth year, the music "Yuanhe" has six changes to bring down the Heavenly Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-ninth year the Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized: "According to the elegant music fixed on the day of the eastern feng at Mount Tai in the twelfth year, Yuanhe has six changes to bring down the Heavenly Spirit.

sentences.zh: 《順和》八變，以降地祇。

translations.literal: "Shunhe" has eight changes to bring down the Earth Spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Shunhe has eight changes to bring down the Earth Spirits.

sentences.zh: 皇帝行，用《太和》之樂。

translations.literal: When the emperor processed, use the music "Taihe."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor processed, use Taihe.

sentences.zh: 其封太山也，登歌、奠玉幣，用《肅和》之樂；

translations.literal: At the feng of Mount Tai, for ascent hymn and offering of jade disks, use the music "Suhe";
translations.idiomatic: At the feng of Mount Tai, for the ascent hymn and offering of jade disks, use Suhe;

sentences.zh: 迎俎，用《雍和》之樂；

translations.literal: to welcome the offering stands, use the music "Yonghe";
translations.idiomatic: to welcome the offering stands, use Yonghe;

sentences.zh: 酌獻、飲福，用《壽和》之樂；

translations.literal: for libation offering and drinking the blessing, use the music "Shouhe";
translations.idiomatic: for libation offering and drinking the blessing, use Shouhe;

sentences.zh: 送文、迎武，用《舒和》之樂；

translations.literal: to send off the civil and welcome the martial, use the music "Shuhe";
translations.idiomatic: to send off the civil and welcome the martial, use Shuhe;

sentences.zh: 亞獻、終獻，用《凱安》之樂；

translations.literal: for the second and final libations, use the music "Kai'an";
translations.idiomatic: for the second and final libations, use Kai'an;

sentences.zh: 送神，用夾鐘宮《元和》之樂。

translations.literal: to send off the spirits, use Jiazhong-palace "Yuanhe."
translations.idiomatic: to send off the spirits, use Jiazhong-palace Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 神社首也，送神用林鐘宮《順和》之樂。

translations.literal: The spirit shrine is foremost; to send off the spirits use Linzhong-palace "Shunhe."
translations.idiomatic: The spirit shrine is foremost; to send off the spirits use Linzhong-palace Shunhe.

sentences.zh: 享太廟也，迎神用《永和》之樂；

translations.literal: At offerings in the Grand Temple, to welcome the spirits use the music "Yonghe";
translations.idiomatic: At offerings in the Grand Temple, to welcome the spirits use Yonghe;

sentences.zh: 獻祖宣皇帝酌獻用《光大》之舞，懿祖光皇帝酌獻用《長發》之舞，太祖景皇帝酌獻用《大政》之舞，世祖元皇帝酌獻用《大成》之舞，高祖神堯皇帝酌獻用《大明》之舞，太宗文皇帝酌獻用《崇德》之舞，高宗天皇大帝酌獻用《鈞天》之舞，中宗孝和皇帝酌獻用《太和》之舞，睿宗大聖貞皇帝酌獻用《景雲》之舞；

translations.literal: for libation to Offering Ancestor Emperor Xuan perform the dance "Guangda," to Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Guang perform "Changfa," to Founding Ancestor Emperor Jing perform "Dazheng," to World Ancestor Emperor Yuan perform "Dacheng," to High Ancestor Emperor Shenyao perform "Daming," to Founding Ancestor Emperor Wen perform "Chongde," to High Ancestor Emperor Tianhuang perform "Juntian," to Middle Ancestor Emperor Xiaohe perform "Taihe," to Sagacious Ancestor Emperor Dasheng Zhen perform "Jingyun";
translations.idiomatic: for libation to Offering Ancestor Emperor Xuan perform Guangda, to Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Guang perform Changfa, to Founding Ancestor Emperor Jing perform Dazheng, to World Ancestor Emperor Yuan perform Dacheng, to High Ancestor Emperor Shenyao perform Daming, to Founding Ancestor Emperor Wen perform Chongde, to High Ancestor Emperor Tianhuang perform Juntian, to Middle Ancestor Emperor Xiaohe perform Taihe, to Sagacious Ancestor Emperor Dasheng Zhen perform Jingyun;

sentences.zh: 徹豆，用《雍和》之舞；

translations.literal: to remove the beans, perform the dance "Yonghe";
translations.idiomatic: to remove the beans, perform Yonghe;

sentences.zh: 送神，用黃鐘宮《永和》之樂。

translations.literal: to send off the spirits, use Huangzhong-palace "Yonghe."
translations.idiomatic: to send off the spirits, use Huangzhong-palace Yonghe.

sentences.zh: 臣以樂章殘缺，積有歲時。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that the music sections are incomplete and have lacked repair for years.
translations.idiomatic: We consider that the music sections are incomplete and have lacked repair for years.

sentences.zh: 自有事東巡，親謁九廟，聖情慎禮，精祈感通，皆祠前累日考定音律，請編入史冊，萬代施行。

translations.literal: Since the eastern tour and personal audience at the nine temples, the sage sentiment was careful in ritual and refined prayer sensed communion—all several days before sacrifice examining and fixing pitch and tones; we request they be compiled into the historical records for ten thousand generations' practice."
translations.idiomatic: Since the eastern tour and personal audience at the nine temples, the emperor was careful in ritual and refined prayer sensed communion—several days before each sacrifice examining and fixing pitch and tones; we request they be compiled into the historical records for practice in ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 」下制曰：「王公卿士，爰及有司，頻詣闕上言，請以『唐樂』為名者，斯至公之事，朕安得而辭焉。

translations.literal: The issued ordinance said: "Princes, dukes, ministers, and scholars, reaching to the responsible offices, have repeatedly come to the gate and memorialized, requesting that 'Tang music' be the name—this is a matter of utmost impartiality; how could We decline?
translations.idiomatic: The issued ordinance said: "Princes, dukes, ministers, and scholars, down to the responsible offices, have repeatedly come to the gate and memorialized, requesting that 'Tang music' be the name—this is a matter of utmost impartiality; how could We decline?

sentences.zh: 然則《大咸》、《大韶》、《大濩》、《大夏》，皆以大字表其樂章，今之所定，宜曰《大唐樂》。

translations.literal: Yet "Daxian," "Dashao," "Dahu," and "Daxia" all used the character da to mark their music sections; what is now fixed should be called "Great Tang Music."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Daxian, Dashao, Dahu, and Daxia all used the character da to mark their music sections; what is now fixed should be called Great Tang Music."

sentences.zh: 」皇祖弘農府君至高祖大武皇帝六廟，貞觀中已詔顏師古等定樂章舞號。

translations.literal: From Imperial Grandfather Hongnong through the High Ancestor Great Martial Emperor's six temples—in the Zhenguan era an edict had already ordered Yan Shigu and others to fix music sections and dance names.
translations.idiomatic: From Imperial Grandfather Hongnong through the High Ancestor Great Martial Emperor's six temples—in Zhenguan an edict had already ordered Yan Shigu and others to fix music sections and dance names.

sentences.zh: 洎今太常寺又奏有司所定獻祖宣皇帝至睿宗聖貞皇帝九廟酌獻用舞之號。

translations.literal: By now the Court of Imperial Sacrifices again memorialized the offices' fixing of libation dances from Offering Ancestor Emperor Xuan through the Sagacious Ancestor Emperor Zhen's nine temples.
translations.idiomatic: By now the Court of Imperial Sacrifices again reported the offices' fixing of libation dances from Offering Ancestor Emperor Xuan through the Sagacious Ancestor Emperor Zhen's nine temples.

sentences.zh: 四月，命有司定玄元皇帝廟告享所奏樂，降神用《混成》之樂，送神用《太一》之樂。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the offices were ordered to fix the music performed at report-offerings in the temple of the Primordial Origin Emperor; to bring down the spirit use the music "Huncheng," to send off the spirit use the music "Taiyi."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the offices were ordered to fix the music at report-offerings in the temple of the Primordial Origin Emperor; to bring down the spirit use Huncheng, to send off the spirit use Taiyi.

sentences.zh: 六月，有司奏：「玄宗廟樂請奏《廣運》之舞，肅宗廟樂請奏《惟新》之舞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the offices memorialized: "For the Mystical Ancestor's temple music please perform the dance "Guangyun"; for the Solemn Ancestor's temple music please perform the dance "Weixin."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the offices memorialized: "For the Mystical Ancestor's temple music please perform Guangyun; for the Solemn Ancestor's temple music please perform Weixin."

sentences.zh: 」，代宗廟樂請奏《保大》之舞。

translations.literal: For the Generation Ancestor's temple music please perform the dance "Baoda."
translations.idiomatic: For the Generation Ancestor's temple music please perform Baoda.

sentences.zh: 十月，德宗廟樂請奏《文明》之舞。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Virtuous Ancestor's temple music—please perform the dance "Wenming."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, for the Virtuous Ancestor's temple music please perform Wenming.

sentences.zh: ，順宗廟樂請奏《大順》之舞。

translations.literal: For the Compliance Ancestor's temple music please perform the dance "Dashun."
translations.idiomatic: For the Compliance Ancestor's temple music please perform Dashun.

sentences.zh: ，憲宗廟樂請奏《象德》之舞。

translations.literal: For the Accomplished Ancestor's temple music please perform the dance "Xiangde."
translations.idiomatic: For the Accomplished Ancestor's temple music please perform Xiangde.

sentences.zh: 穆宗廟樂請奏《和寧》之舞。

translations.literal: For Emperor Muzong's temple music please perform the dance "Hening."
translations.idiomatic: For Emperor Muzong's temple music please perform Hening.

sentences.zh: 敬宗廟樂請奏《大鈞》之舞。

translations.literal: For the Respectful Ancestor's temple music please perform the dance "Dajun."
translations.idiomatic: For the Respectful Ancestor's temple music please perform Dajun.

sentences.zh: 文宗廟樂請奏《文成》之舞。

translations.literal: For the Cultured Ancestor's temple music please perform the dance "Wencheng."
translations.idiomatic: For the Cultured Ancestor's temple music please perform Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 武宗廟樂請奏《大定》之舞。

translations.literal: For the Martial Ancestor's temple music please perform the dance "Dading."
translations.idiomatic: For the Martial Ancestor's temple music please perform Dading.

sentences.zh: ，宴群臣，始奏秦王破陣之曲。

translations.literal: At a banquet for the assembled ministers, they first performed the tune "Prince of Qin Breaking the Battle Array."
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet for the assembled ministers they first performed the tune Prince of Qin Breaking the Battle Array.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂侍臣曰：「朕昔在籓，屢有征討，世間遂有此樂，豈意今日登于雅樂。

translations.literal: Taizong told the attending ministers: "In former days when I was in the fief I repeatedly had campaigns; the world thereby got this music—who would have thought today it would ascend to elegant music!
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told the attending ministers: "When I was in the fief I repeatedly campaigned; the world thereby got this music—who would have thought it would today ascend to elegant music!

sentences.zh: 然其發揚蹈厲，雖異文容，功業由之，致有今日，所以被于樂章，示不忘於本也。

translations.literal: Yet its display of vigor and tread, though differing from cultured bearing, the achievement came by it to reach today; therefore it is clothed in music sections—to show not forgetting the root."
translations.idiomatic: Yet its display of vigor and tread, though unlike cultured bearing, achievement came by it to reach today; therefore it is clothed in music sections—to show we do not forget our root."

sentences.zh: 」尚書右僕射封德彝進曰：「陛下以聖武戡難，立極安人，功成化定，陳樂象德，實弘濟之盛烈，為將來之壯觀。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Feng Deyi advanced, saying: "Your Majesty with sage martial quelled difficulty, established the pole and settled the people; achievement complete and transformation fixed, displaying music to image virtue—truly a magnificent achievement of succoring the age, a grand sight for generations to come.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Feng Deyi advanced: "Your Majesty with sage martial quelled difficulty, established the pole and settled the people; achievement complete and transformation fixed, displaying music to image virtue—truly a magnificent achievement of succoring the age, a grand sight for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 文容習儀，豈得為比。

translations.literal: Cultured bearing and practiced ritual—how could they compare!
translations.idiomatic: Cultured bearing and practiced ritual—how could they be compared!

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「朕雖以武功定天下，終當以文德綏海內。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Though I settled all under Heaven by martial achievement, in the end I shall soothe the seas within by cultured virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "Though I settled the realm by martial achievement, in the end I shall soothe the seas within by cultured virtue.

sentences.zh: 文武之道，各隨其時，公謂文容不如蹈厲，斯為過矣。

translations.literal: The ways of wen and wu each follow their time; you say cultured bearing is not equal to vigorous tread—that is excessive."
translations.idiomatic: The ways of civil and martial each follow their time; you say cultured bearing is not equal to vigorous tread—that goes too far."

sentences.zh: 」德彝頓首曰：「臣不敏，不足以知之。

translations.literal: Deyi bowed his head, saying: "Your servant is not acute and is insufficient to know this."
translations.idiomatic: Deyi bowed his head: "Your servant is not acute and is insufficient to know this."

sentences.zh: 」其後令魏徵、虞世南、褚亮、李百藥改制歌辭，更名《七德》之舞，增舞者至百二十人，被甲執戟，以象戰陣之法焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter he ordered Wei Zheng, Yu Shinan, Chu Liang, and Li Baiyao to revise the song texts, renaming it the dance "Qide," increasing dancers to one hundred twenty, donning armor and grasping halberds to image battle-array methods.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he ordered Wei Zheng, Yu Shinan, Chu Liang, and Li Baiyao to revise the song texts, renaming it the dance Qide, increasing dancers to one hundred twenty, donning armor and grasping halberds to image battle-array methods.

sentences.zh: 六年，太宗行幸慶善宮，宴從臣于渭水之濱，賦詩十韻。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Taizong traveled in person to Qingshan Palace and banqueted his following ministers on the Wei River's bank, composing a poem in ten rhymes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Taizong went in person to Qingshan Palace and banqueted his ministers on the Wei River's bank, composing a poem in ten rhymes.

sentences.zh: 其宮即太宗降誕之所。

translations.literal: That palace was where Taizong was born.
translations.idiomatic: That palace was Taizong's birthplace.

sentences.zh: 車駕臨幸，每特感慶，賞賜閭裏，有同漢之宛、沛焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage visited in person he was especially moved with celebration, bestowing gifts on the hamlet—like Han's Wan and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the imperial carriage visited he was especially moved with celebration, bestowing gifts on the hamlet—like Han's Wan and Pei.

sentences.zh: 於是起居郎呂才以禦制詩等於樂府，被之管弦，名為《功成慶善樂》之曲，令童兒八佾，皆進德冠、紫袴褶，為《九功》之舞。

translations.literal: Thereupon Attendant for Drafting Lü Cai set the imperial poems to the Music Bureau, clothed them in strings and pipes, naming the tune "Achievement Complete, Qingshan Celebration," ordering eight rows of children all wearing jinde caps and purple trousers and jackets, performing the dance "Jiugong."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Attendant for Drafting Lü Cai set the imperial poems to the Music Bureau, clothed them in strings and pipes, naming the tune Achievement Complete, Qingshan Celebration, ordering eight rows of children all wearing jinde caps and purple trousers and jackets, performing the dance Jiugong.

sentences.zh: 冬至享宴，及國有大慶，與《七德》之舞皆奏於庭。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice feast and when the state had great celebration, together with the dance "Qide" they were all performed in the court.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice feast and when the state had great celebration, together with the dance Qide they were all performed in the court.

sentences.zh: 七年，太宗制《破陣舞圖》：左圓右方，先偏後伍，魚麗鵝貫，箕張翼舒，交錯屈伸，首尾回互，以象戰陣之形。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Taizong devised the "Battle-Array Dance Diagram": left round, right square, first echelon then five-deep, fish-scale and goose-file, winnow-spread and wing-unfold, interlaced bending and stretching, head and tail turning back upon each other—to image the battle array's form.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Taizong devised the Battle-Array Dance Diagram: left round, right square, first echelon then five-deep, fish-scale and goose-file, winnow-spread and wing-unfold, interlaced bending and stretching, head and tail turning back upon each other—to image the battle array's form.

sentences.zh: 令呂才依圖教樂工百二十人，被甲執戟而習之。

translations.literal: He ordered Lü Cai according to the diagram to teach one hundred twenty music workers, donning armor and grasping halberds to practice it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Lü Cai to teach one hundred twenty music workers from the diagram, donning armor and grasping halberds to practice it.

sentences.zh: 凡為三變，每變為四陣，有來往疾徐擊刺之象，以應歌節，數日而就，更名《七德》之舞。

translations.literal: In all there were three changes; each change was four arrays, with coming and going, fast and slow, striking and thrusting images to match the song's beats—in several days it was done, and the name was changed to the dance "Qide."
translations.idiomatic: In all there were three changes; each change was four arrays, with coming and going, fast and slow, striking and thrusting images to match the song's beats—in several days it was done, and the name was changed to the dance Qide.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，奏《七德》、《九功》之舞，觀者見其抑揚蹈厲，莫不扼腕踴躍，凜然震竦。

translations.literal: On day guisi they performed the dances "Qide" and "Jiugong"; viewers seeing their restraint and vigorous tread all clutched their wrists and leapt, awestruck and trembling.
translations.idiomatic: On day guisi they performed the dances Qide and Jiugong; viewers seeing their restraint and vigorous tread all clutched their wrists and leapt, awestruck and trembling.

sentences.zh: 武臣列將咸上壽云：「此舞皆是陛下百戰百勝之形容。

translations.literal: Martial ministers and arrayed generals all raised cups for longevity, saying: "This dance is entirely Your Majesty's image of a hundred battles, a hundred victories."
translations.idiomatic: Martial ministers and arrayed generals all raised cups for longevity, saying: "This dance is entirely Your Majesty's likeness in a hundred battles and a hundred victories."

sentences.zh: 」群臣咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers all called "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers all shouted "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 蠻夷十餘種自請率舞，詔許之，久而乃罷。

translations.literal: More than ten kinds of southern barbarians themselves requested to lead the dance; an edict permitted it, and only after a long while did it cease.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten southern peoples themselves requested to lead the dance; an edict permitted it, and only after a long while did it stop.

sentences.zh: 十四年，有景雲見，河水清。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year there appeared an auspicious cloud and the Yellow River cleared.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year an auspicious cloud appeared and the Yellow River cleared.

sentences.zh: 張文收采古《朱雁》、《天馬》之義，製《景雲河清歌》，名曰宴樂，奏之管弦，為諸樂之首，元會第一奏者是也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenshou gathered the ancient meaning of "Vermilion Goose" and "Heavenly Horse," composing the "Jingyun River Clear Song," naming it banquet music; performed on strings and pipes, it was first among all music—the first performed at the great assembly was this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenshou gathered the ancient meaning of Vermilion Goose and Heavenly Horse, composing the Jingyun River Clear Song, naming it banquet music; performed on strings and pipes, it was first among all music—the first performed at the great assembly was this.

sentences.zh: 十一月，高宗親祀南郊，黃門侍郎宇文節奏言：「依儀，明日朝群臣，除樂懸，請奏《九部樂》。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the High Ancestor personally sacrificed at the southern suburb; Yellow Gate Vice Director Yu Wenjie memorialized, saying: "According to the ritual, tomorrow at audience with the assembled ministers, removing the music suspension, please perform the "Nine Department Music."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the High Ancestor personally sacrificed at the southern suburb; Yellow Gate Vice Director Yu Wenjie memorialized: "According to the ritual, tomorrow at audience with the assembled ministers, removing the music suspension, please perform the Nine Department Music."

sentences.zh: 」上因曰：「《破陣樂舞》者，情不忍觀，所司更不宜設。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon said: "As for the 'Breaking the Array' dance—emotionally I cannot bear to watch it; the offices should furthermore not set it up."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon said: "As for the Breaking the Array dance—emotionally I cannot bear to watch it; the offices should furthermore not set it up."

sentences.zh: 」言畢，慘愴久之。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark. When he had finished speaking, he remained deeply grieved for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished, he grieved a long while.

sentences.zh: 正月，改《破陣樂舞》為《神功破陣樂》。

translations.literal: In the first month, the Breaking-the-Array dance was renamed Divine Merit in Breaking the Array.
translations.idiomatic: First month: Breaking-the-Array dance renamed Divine Merit in Breaking the Array.

sentences.zh: 二年，太常奏《白雪》琴曲。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices presented the zither piece White Snow.
translations.idiomatic: Second year: the Court presented the zither piece White Snow.

sentences.zh: 先是，上以琴中雅曲，古人歌之，近代已來，此聲頓絕，雖有傳習，又失宮商，令所司簡樂工解琴笙者修習舊曲。

translations.literal: Earlier, because the emperor knew that elegant zither pieces in antiquity were sung but in recent times this practice had abruptly ceased, and though some transmission survived the modes were wrong, he ordered the relevant offices to select music workers skilled at zither and mouth-organ to restore the old pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor, knowing ancient elegant zither pieces were sung but the practice had died out and surviving versions had wrong pitches, ordered skilled zither and mouth-organ workers to restore the old repertoire.

sentences.zh: 至是太常上言曰：「臣謹按《禮記》、《家語》云：舜彈五弦之琴，歌《南風》之詩。

translations.literal: At this time the Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized: "Your servant respectfully notes that the Book of Rites and the Household Sayings state: Shun played the five-string zither and sang the Ode to the Southern Breeze.
translations.idiomatic: The Court then memorialized: "Per the Book of Rites and Household Sayings, Shun played the five-string zither and sang the Ode to the Southern Breeze.

sentences.zh: 是知琴操曲弄，皆合於歌。

translations.literal: Hence one knows that zither performance and melody all accord with song.
translations.idiomatic: Thus zither pieces and melodies were all meant to be sung.

sentences.zh: 又張華《博物志》云：『《白雪》是大帝使素女鼓五十弦瑟曲名。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhang Hua's Comprehensive Record states: "White Snow was the name of a fifty-string se piece that the Plain Girl played at the Supreme Emperor's command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua's Comprehensive Record also says: "White Snow was a fifty-string se piece the Plain Girl played for the Supreme Emperor.

sentences.zh: 』又楚大夫宋玉對襄王云：『有客於郢中歌《陽春白雪》，國中和者數十人。

translations.literal: " The Chu grandee Song Yu also told King Xiang of Chu: "A guest in Ying sang Sunny Spring and White Snow; only a few dozen in the state could join in harmony."
translations.idiomatic: Song Yu told King Xiang: "A guest in Ying sang Sunny Spring and White Snow; only a few dozen could harmonize."

sentences.zh: 』是知《白雪》琴曲，本宜合歌，以其調高，人和遂寡。

translations.literal: " Hence the zither piece White Snow was originally meant to be sung; because its mode was high, harmonizers were few.
translations.idiomatic: So White Snow was meant to be sung; its mode was so high that few could join in.

sentences.zh: 自宋玉以後，迄今千祀，未有能歌《白雪曲》者。

translations.literal: From Song Yu until now, a full millennium has passed with no one able to sing the White Snow melody.
translations.idiomatic: Since Song Yu, a thousand years have passed with no one able to sing White Snow.

sentences.zh: 臣今准敕，依於琴中舊曲，定其宮商，然後教習，併合於歌。

translations.literal: Your servant now, pursuant to the edict, relying on the old pieces on the zither, has fixed their modes, then taught them, combining them with song.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuant to the edict I fixed the modes of the old zither pieces, taught them, and set them to song.

sentences.zh: 輒以御製《雪詩》為《白雪》歌辭。

translations.literal: I take the imperially composed Snow Poems as the lyrics for White Snow.
translations.idiomatic: I used the imperial Snow Poems as White Snow's lyrics.

sentences.zh: 又按古今樂府，奏正曲之後，皆別有送聲，君唱臣和，事彰前史。

translations.literal: Moreover, examining ancient and modern Music Bureau pieces, after the main melody is played there is always a separate sending-off vocal; lord sings and ministers respond—a fact plain in earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient and modern Music Bureau pieces also had sending-off vocals after the main tune—lord sings, ministers answer—as earlier histories show.

sentences.zh: 輒取侍臣等奉和雪詩以為送聲，各十六節，今悉教訖，並皆諧韻。

translations.literal: I take the attendant ministers' responsive snow poems as the sending-off vocals, each of sixteen stanzas; all have now been taught to completion and all rhyme properly."
translations.idiomatic: I took the ministers' responsive snow poems as sending-off vocals, sixteen stanzas each; all are taught and rhyme correctly."

sentences.zh: 」上善之，乃付太常編於樂府。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and had the Court of Imperial Sacrifices compile them into the Music Bureau repertoire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and had the Court enter them in the Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，太常丞呂才造琴歌《白雪》等曲，上製歌辭十六首，編入樂府。

translations.literal: Second month of the sixth year, Vice Director of the Court Lü Cai composed zither songs including White Snow; the emperor wrote sixteen sets of lyrics, entered into the Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, second month: Lü Cai composed zither songs including White Snow; the emperor wrote sixteen lyrics, entered in the Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，上欲伐遼，于屯營教舞，召李義府、任雅相、許敬宗、許圉師、張延師、蘇定方、阿史那忠、于闐王伏闍、上官儀等，赴洛城門觀樂。

translations.literal: Third month of the sixth year, as the emperor planned to campaign against Liaodong, he had dance taught at the encampment and summoned Li Yifu, Ren Yaxiang, Xu Jingzong, Xu Yuanshi, Zhang Yanshi, Su Dingfang, Ashina Zhong, the King of Khotan Fuzhe, Shangguan Yi, and others to Luoyang Gate to view the performance.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, third month: planning the Liaodong campaign, he taught dance at camp and summoned Li Yifu, Ren Yaxiang, Xu Jingzong, Xu Yuanshi, Zhang Yanshi, Su Dingfang, Ashina Zhong, the King of Khotan Fuzhe, Shangguan Yi, and others to Luoyang Gate to watch.

sentences.zh: 樂名《一戎大定樂》。

translations.literal: The piece was titled One Campaign, Great Settlement.
translations.idiomatic: The piece was One Campaign, Great Settlement.

sentences.zh: 賜觀樂者雜彩有差。

translations.literal: Those granted to view were given brocade silks of varying grades.
translations.idiomatic: Viewers received brocade silks of varying grades.

sentences.zh: 十月，制曰：「國家平定天下，革命創制，紀功旌德，久被樂章。

translations.literal: Tenth month, edict: "The state having pacified the realm and transformed institutions through revolution, recording merit and displaying virtue has long been clothed in music.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, edict: "Having pacified the realm and remade institutions, recording merit in music is long established.

sentences.zh: 今郊祀四懸，猶用干戚之舞，先朝作樂，韜而未伸。

translations.literal: Yet at suburban sacrifice the four suspended sets still use shield-and-axe dances; music composed by prior courts lies wrapped away and unperformed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet suburban sacrifice still uses shield-and-axe dance on the four suspensions; prior courts' music lies stored and unperformed.

sentences.zh: 其郊廟享宴等所奏宮懸，文舞宜用《功成慶善》之樂，皆著履執拂，依舊服袴褶、童子冠。

translations.literal: For palace suspended music at suburban and temple feasts and banquets, civil dance should use Merit Achieved, Celebration of Goodness, all wearing shoes, holding fly-whisks, in the former dress of trousers and jackets and youths' caps.
translations.idiomatic: Palace suspended civil dance at suburban and temple rites and banquets should use Merit Achieved, Celebration of Goodness—shoes, fly-whisks, former trousers-and-jacket dress and youths' caps.

sentences.zh: 其武舞宜用《神功破陣》之樂，皆被甲持戟，其執纛之人，亦著金甲。

translations.literal: Military dance should use Divine Merit in Breaking the Array, all in armor holding halberds; those bearing banners also wear gilded armor.
translations.idiomatic: Military dance should use Divine Merit in Breaking the Array—armor and halberds; banner bearers also wear gilded armor.

sentences.zh: 人數並依八佾，仍量加簫、笛、歌鼓等，並于懸南列坐，若舞即與宮懸合奏。

translations.literal: Personnel as in the eight rows of dancers; add bamboo pipes, flutes, song-drums, etc., seated in a line south of the suspension; when they dance they play together with the palace suspended orchestra.
translations.idiomatic: Numbers as in eight rows; add pipes, flutes, and song-drums south of the suspension; when they dance they join the palace suspended orchestra.

sentences.zh: 其宴樂內二色舞者，仍依舊別設。

translations.literal: The two-color dancers within banquets remain separately arranged as before."
translations.idiomatic: Banquet two-color dancers remain separately arranged as before."

sentences.zh: 」十一月敕：「供祠祭《上元舞》，前令大祠享皆將陳設。

translations.literal: Eleventh month edict: "Provision of the Shangyuan dance for sacrificial rites was formerly ordered for all major shrine offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month edict: "The Shangyuan dance for sacrifices was formerly set for all major shrine offerings.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，圓丘方澤，大廟祠享，然後用此舞，餘祭並停。

translations.literal: From now on, it shall be used only for offerings at the Round Mound, Square Mound, and Grand Temple; all other sacrifices shall cease using it."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter use it only at Round Mound, Square Mound, and Grand Temple offerings; stop it at other sacrifices."

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark.
translations.idiomatic: End of edict.

sentences.zh: 十一月六日，太常少卿韋萬石奏曰：「據《貞觀禮》，郊享日文舞奏《豫和》、《順和》、《永和》等樂，其舞人著委貌冠服，並手執籥翟。

translations.literal: Sixth day of the eleventh month, Vice Director of the Court Wei Wanshi memorialized: "According to the Zhenguan rites code, at suburban offering civil dance performs Joyful Harmony, Smooth Harmony, Eternal Harmony, etc.; dancers wear weimao caps and robes, all holding yue flutes and pheasant feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, sixth day: Vice Director Wei Wanshi memorialized: "Per Zhenguan rites, suburban civil dance uses Joyful Harmony, Smooth Harmony, Eternal Harmony; dancers wear weimao caps and robes with yue flutes and pheasant feathers.

sentences.zh: 其武舞奏《凱安》，其舞人並著平冕，手執干戚。

translations.literal: Military dance performs Triumphant Peace; dancers all wear pingmian caps and hold shields and axes.
translations.idiomatic: Military dance uses Triumphant Peace; dancers wear pingmian caps with shields and axes.

sentences.zh: 奉十月敕，文舞改用《功成慶善樂》，武舞改用《神功破陣樂》，並改器服等。

translations.literal: Pursuant to the tenth-month edict, civil dance is changed to Merit Achieved, Celebration of Goodness; military dance to Divine Merit in Breaking the Array, with changed implements and dress.
translations.idiomatic: Per the tenth-month edict, civil dance becomes Merit Achieved, Celebration of Goodness and military dance Divine Merit in Breaking the Array, with changed implements and dress.

sentences.zh: 自奉敕以來，為《慶善樂》不可降神，《神功破陣樂》未入雅樂，雖改用器服，其舞猶依舊，迄今不改。

translations.literal: Since receiving the edict, because Celebration of Goodness cannot summon the spirits and Divine Merit in Breaking the Array is not yet in elegant music, though implements and dress were changed the dances remain as before and to this day have not been altered.
translations.idiomatic: Since the edict, Celebration of Goodness cannot summon spirits and Divine Merit in Breaking the Array is not yet elegant music; though dress changed, the dances remain old and unaltered.

sentences.zh: 事既不安，恐須別有處分者。

translations.literal: The matter being unsettled, perhaps separate disposition is needed."
translations.idiomatic: The matter is unsettled; separate disposition may be needed."

sentences.zh: 」以今月六日錄奏，奉敕：「舊文舞、武舞既不可廢，並器服總宜依舊。

translations.literal: Recorded and memorialized on the sixth of this month; edict: "The former civil and military dances cannot be abolished; all implements and dress should in general follow the old way.
translations.idiomatic: Recorded sixth of this month; edict: "Former civil and military dances cannot be abolished; implements and dress should follow the old way.

sentences.zh: 若懸作《上元舞》日，仍奏《神功破陣樂》及《功成慶善樂》，並殿庭用舞，並須引出懸外作。

translations.literal: On days when the Shangyuan dance is suspended, still perform Divine Merit in Breaking the Array and Merit Achieved, Celebration of Goodness; court dances must all be performed outside the suspended set.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shangyuan dance is suspended, still perform Divine Merit in Breaking the Array and Merit Achieved, Celebration of Goodness; court dances must be performed outside the suspension.

sentences.zh: 其安置舞曲，宜更商量作安穩法。

translations.literal: The placement of dance pieces should be reconsidered for a secure method.
translations.idiomatic: Dance placement should be reconsidered for a stable arrangement.

sentences.zh: 並錄《凱安》六變法象奏聞。

translations.literal: Also record the six changes of Triumphant Peace and their symbolism and report."
translations.idiomatic: Also record Triumphant Peace's six changes and their symbolism and report."

sentences.zh: 」萬石又與刊正官等奏曰：

translations.literal: Wanshi again submitted with the collation officials, etc.:
translations.idiomatic: Wanshi again submitted with the collation officials:

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The edict was assented to.
translations.idiomatic: Assent was given.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，上在九成宮咸亨殿宴集，有韓王元嘉、霍王元軌及南北軍將軍等。

translations.literal: Seventh month, third year, the emperor feasted at Jiucheng Palace in the Xianheng Hall; Han Prince Yuanjia, Huo Prince Yuan gui, and generals of the northern and southern armies were present.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, seventh month: the emperor feasted at Jiucheng Palace, Xianheng Hall, with Han Prince Yuanjia, Huo Prince Yuan gui, and northern and southern army generals.

sentences.zh: 樂作，太常少卿韋萬石奏稱：「《破陣樂舞》者，是皇祚發跡所由，宣揚宗祖盛烈，傳之於後，永永無窮。

translations.literal: When music began, Vice Director Wei Wanshi memorialized: "The Breaking-the-Array dance is where the imperial fortune took its start; it proclaims the ancestors' glorious achievements, transmitted to posterity without end.
translations.idiomatic: As music began, Wei Wanshi memorialized: "Breaking-the-Array is where imperial fortune began; it proclaims ancestral glory to endless posterity.

sentences.zh: 自天皇臨馭四海，寢而不作，既緣聖情感愴，群下無敢關言。

translations.literal: Since the August Sovereign came to rule all within the four seas it has lain dormant; because the sage's feeling was mournful, no one below dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Since the August Sovereign ruled the four seas it has lain dormant; the sage's grief was such that none below dared speak.

sentences.zh: 臣忝職樂司，廢缺是懼。

translations.literal: Your servant, holding office in the Music Office, fears neglect and lapse.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant in the Music Office fears neglect.

sentences.zh: 依禮，祭之日，天子親總干戚以舞先祖之樂，與天下同樂之也，今《破陣樂》久廢，群下無所稱述，將何以發孝思之情？

translations.literal: By rite, on the day of sacrifice the Son of Heaven personally leads shield and axe to dance the music of the ancestors, sharing joy with the world; now Breaking the Array has long been abandoned and those below have nothing to cite—how can filial thought be aroused?"
translations.idiomatic: By rite the Son of Heaven on sacrifice day leads shield and axe to dance ancestral music and share joy with the realm; Breaking the Array is long abandoned—how can filial feeling be stirred?"

sentences.zh: 」上矍然改容，俯遂所請，有制令奏樂舞。

translations.literal: The emperor started, changed expression, bowed to grant the request, and ordered the dance performed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started, changed expression, granted the request, and ordered the dance.

sentences.zh: 既畢，上欷歔感咽，涕泗交流，臣下悲淚，莫能仰視。

translations.literal: When it ended the emperor sighed with feeling, tears streaming; the ministers wept and could not look up.
translations.idiomatic: When it ended the emperor sighed, tears streaming; ministers wept and could not look up.

sentences.zh: 久之，顧謂兩王曰：「不見此樂，垂三十年，乍此觀聽，實深哀感。

translations.literal: After a long while he turned to the two princes and said: "I have not seen this dance for nearly thirty years; suddenly viewing it today truly stirs deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: After long silence he told the two princes: "Nearly thirty years without this dance; seeing it today stirs deep grief.

sentences.zh: 追思往日，王業艱難勤苦若此，朕今嗣守洪業，可忘武功？

translations.literal: Recalling past days, the royal enterprise was arduous and toilsome like this; I now inherit and guard the great enterprise—can I forget military achievement?"
translations.idiomatic: Recalling the past, the royal enterprise was toilsome like this; I now guard the great enterprise—can I forget martial achievement?"
